subject: Production timeouts causing customer impact — request for executive brief & action plan
messages:
From: Maria Alvarez <maria@finio.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, eng-team@finio.com
Date: 2027-04-11T08:12:00Z
Subject: Severe timeouts and 5xx/429s affecting Finio checkout (urgent)

Soojin / Redwood team,

We're seeing a large spike of timeouts and 5xx/429 errors across our checkout flows starting ~07:45 UTC. This is impacting a subset of high-volume merchants and increasing abandonment. Attached are a short set of server logs and a screenshot of your Grafana dashboard for our account. We have customers in chargeback windows and sales are getting escalations.

Quick facts from our side:
- Window: ~07:45–08:05 UTC
- Error mix: 429 + 500s (tokenization/response generation timeouts)
- Symptoms: long tail latency, many client-side retries, a noticeable retry storm around 07:50

We need immediate mitigation (rate limits, fallback to smaller model, or capacity bump) and an executive-level update. Please treat as Sev1 for Finio.

--
Maria Alvarez
VP Engineering, Finio Payments
maria@finio.com
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Maria Alvarez <maria@finio.com>, eng-team@finio.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T08:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Severe timeouts and 5xx/429s affecting Finio checkout (urgent)

Maria — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. We're treating as Sev1. I'm standing up a small war room with ops/infra now. Immediate next steps:

1) Short-term mitigation (next 15m): enable per-customer throttling and route Finio traffic to a lower-cost but higher-throughput model variant.
2) Investigation: capture request traces and KV cache miss rates for the 07:30–08:15 window.
3) Exec update: I'll send a brief within 90 minutes with impact and proposed actions.

Marissa / Jonas / Sean — joining you to confirm mitigations and who will own which items. I'll also open a ticket to track the post-incident follow-ups.

Date: 2027-04-11T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Severe timeouts and 5xx/429s affecting Finio checkout (urgent)

Quick ops snapshot from the war room (07:30–08:20):
- Root symptom: sharp KV cache eviction at 07:48 due to a heavy prefix churn pattern from Finio's traffic; this increased per-request compute and evicted cached prefixes used by highest-volume merchants.
- Secondary: client-side SDKs from Finio retried aggressively (3 immediate retries, no jitter) producing a retry amplification starting 07:50.
- Alerts: internal 429 alert threshold didn't trigger until 07:58 (gap). The latency-slo composite alert was configured on p95 only — p99 spike was missed in time.

Mitigations applied by 08:05 UTC:
- Forced route to a quantized high-throughput variant for Finio (reduced p99 by ~350ms).
- Applied immediate per-customer QPS throttle at the edge for Finio to damp retries.

Impact summary: estimated 12% of Finio checkout attempts saw error or timeout; revenue exposure: ~10k USD in the window.

Attachments: finio_error_samples.log; grafana_5xx_chart.png

Cc: Maria Alvarez <maria@finio.com>, eng-team@finio.com
Date: 2027-04-11T12:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Production timeouts — short-term fixes applied; ask for capacity & runbooks

Executive summary for leadership:
- What happened: Kv cache churn + aggressive client retries produced a retry storm which exhausted token-serving slots and caused elevated 429/500s and timeouts.
- Why alerts failed: our alarming threshold used p95 latency and aggregate 429 rate; both were insufficient to detect p99 tail events and per-customer spikes.
- Immediate mitigations: routing to a higher-throughput quantized variant + edge throttles reduced p99 and surface errors.

Recommended executive decisions / asks (need approvals within 24h):
1) Approve temporary Dedicated burst capacity + short-term capping for Finio (30% extra headroom for next 72h) — PROD cost impact estimated: $5k/day.
2) Approve a one-week priority for a runbook + per-customer SLO/alerting changes to be pushed (owner: Jonas).
3) Sales/CS ask: communicate to Finio PM and legal that we are reviewing SLA credits — request requires exec sign-off (owner: Soojin / Sales lead).

I will also open a post-incident RCA doc and populate timeline + first-draft action items.

Subject: Post-incident summary & action tracker — Finio outage (Apr 11)

Folks — thank you for the fast response. Attaching a short executive brief (draft_sla_exception.pdf) and the RCA link. Below is a condensed post-incident summary and the committed actions with owners and target dates.

High-level impact:
- Window: 2027-04-11 07:45–08:10 UTC
- Customer impact: ~12% checkout failures for Finio during window; quick mitigations brought errors down by 08:10.
- Business exposure: ~10k USD estimated. Finio has asked for a formal update and SLA discussion.

Root causes (short):
1) Hot-prefix churn from client's workload drove KV cache evictions and higher per-request work.
2) Finio SDKs retried aggressively without jitter, amplifying load during the tail spike.
3) Alerting/configuration gap: p99 tail and per-customer 429s lacked sufficient coverage.

Committed actions (owner — due):
- Create per-customer alerting runbook template (Marissa Cole — 2027-04-18)
- Add p99 latency and per-customer 429 rate to default SLO alerting (Jonas Weber — 2027-04-15)
- SDK best-practices doc for partners (Customer Solutions) + rollout checklist (Soojin Lee — 2027-04-20)
- Short-term Dedicated burst capacity for Finio approved pending CFO sign-off; apply for 72h window (Soojin Lee / Finance — 2027-04-12)
- Postmortem writeup + exec slide deck for Finio leadership (Soojin Lee — 2027-04-13)

Notes / follow-ups:
- Marissa: please include a timeline of key metric inflection points in the RCA doc (KV miss rate, retry counts, p99 latency) — link above.
- Jonas: please estimate cost impact for the 72h burst and a longer-term sustained headroom proposal by EOD tomorrow.
- Maria / Finio: we will share the exec slide by 2027-04-13 and propose a call to discuss SLA remediation and credits.
